sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Kratom is an evergreen tree of humid forests from Southeast Asia to New Guinea. It often grows 4–9 m tall, sometimes more, in wet lowlands and riverine habitats.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The opposite, broad, stalked leaves are often about 17 × 10 cm and have curved secondary veins. Small pale yellow flowers are grouped in globose heads near the branch tips.

sections.title: Uses and risks
sections.text: The leaves have traditional uses, but kratom can cause serious effects, including liver injury, seizures and substance use disorder. It should not be presented as a safe treatment or recommended for consumption.
